Definition: Distance between transmission and reception (Haversine distance).
Carrier frequency of the transmitted signal.
Effective isotropic radiated power at the transmitter.
Height of the transmitter antenna above ground level.
Height of the receiver antenna above ground level.
Average slope between the transmission point and the point 50 m after reception along the Tx to Rx direction.
Rugosity (standard deviation of elevations) between the transmitter and the point 50 m downstream of the receiver along the Tx to Rx direction.
Horizontal angle between true north and the Tx-Rx direction, measured clockwise in the range [0 deg, 360 deg).
Elevation angle of the Tx-Rx line of sight. Positive: downtilt (receiver below transmitter); negative: uptilt (receiver above transmitter).
Binary indicator of line-of-sight between Tx and Rx.
Distance from Tx to the nearest building intercepting the Tx-Rx ray.
Distance from Tx to the nearest tree intercepting the Tx-Rx ray.
Number of buildings whose footprint intersects the first Fresnel ellipsoid of the Tx-Rx link.
Number of trees whose canopy intersects the first Fresnel ellipsoid of the Tx-Rx link.
Number of buildings within a fixed radius (50 m) around the receiver.
Number of trees within a fixed radius (50 m) around the receiver.

Ambient air temperature at the measurement time. Retained (with Rhum) for its established link to atmospheric refractivity; Wdir/Wspd/Pres were dropped as they have no established physical role in point-to-area median-field prediction.
Relative humidity at the measurement time; drives the wet term of atmospheric refractivity together with Temp.
Categorical morphology label: urban Cotonou vs. suburban Kandi.
